Quick Read

Walmart surged 3% and Costco climbed 2% as hotter-than-expected September inflation drove investors into defensive consumer staples stocks.

SPY fell 1% and XRT dropped 0.5%, making Walmart and Costco's gains stand out sharply against a broad market selloff.

Walmart's 41x P/E leaves little margin for error as rising inflation pushes up goods, labor, and benefits costs simultaneously.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Walmart didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat WMT. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

A hotter-than-expected September inflation report is pushing money toward the retailers that sell everyday necessities, and one discount giant is out in front. Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) stock is trading at $115.10, up 3% and leaving WMT shares up 4% year to date (YTD).

Similarly, Costco Wholesale (NASDAQ:COST) stock is at $976.30, up 2%, riding the same defensive bid. Meanwhile, Target (NYSE:TGT) stock is at $153.43, up 0.9%, a softer gain given its discretionary mix.

Those gains stand out on a down day for stocks. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is declining by 1.33%. Retail as a whole is also under pressure, with the SPDR S&P Retail ETF (NYSEARCA:XRT) down 0.5%.

Hot Inflation Report Sends Money Into Staples

September inflation came in above forecasts, and consumer staples held up while the broad market traded lower on the hotter reading. Shoppers were already uneasy heading into the report, with the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index at 51.7 in August. Market swings stayed measured, as the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) sat at 15.27 on October 13, inside its normal range.

Walmart also has company-specific news in the mix. On October 13, the retailer told its U.S. associates it's adding benefits for the coming plan year, including a zero-dollar prescription tier, a rare conditions center of excellence and dedicated paid leave for parents whose newborns need intensive care.

Is COST a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Costco Wholesale Corporation on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on COST. Costco Wholesale Corporation's share was trading at $954.63 as of October 13th 2026. COST's trailing and forward P/E were 45.51 and 40.32 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a retailer pitched as a great investment. COST shares gained 10.70% year to date. Comparable stocks like Target and BJ's Wholesale Club gained 55.49% and 10.60%, respectively, during the same period. Why are retail stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?

How Instacart (CART) Is Bringing Physical AI Into The Grocery Aisle

06photo/Shutterstock.com

In June, we published an article about the 10 Best Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire Richard Chilton and COST ranked #2 in that article. Btw, the #1 stock in that list returned 45.70% since then. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick but COST has barely gained ground. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on COST. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Costco Wholesale Corporation (NASDAQ:COST) operates membership warehouses selling groceries, household goods, appliances, apparel, gasoline, and other products at low markups, backed by high-margin membership fee revenue. This membership model sits at the heart of the investment story: customers pay an annual fee for access to low prices, while Costco Wholesale Corporation uses its buying power to keep markups low and encourage renewals and repeat visits.

Over the trailing twelve months through the third quarter of fiscal 2026, revenue reached $293.6 billion, up 9.0% year over year, while comparable warehouse sales rose 6.6%. That growth comes at a price: the stock trades at about 45.4 times trailing earnings, well above the peer median of roughly 20.5 times, meaning investors are paying a premium on confidence that this membership-driven growth keeps going for years.

The bullish case rests on Costco Wholesale Corporation's membership flywheel, where annual fees, low markups, buying power, and loyal customers reinforce one another. This lets the company grow two ways at once — opening new warehouses and adding members, while also getting existing shoppers to spend more, both in stores and online. Recent numbers back that up: digital sales grew 21% and paid memberships rose 4.1% in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, while return on equity over the trailing twelve months reached 29.2%, showing how efficiently the business converts thin retail margins into strong profitability.

title: OLLI's New $500M Buyback Authorization Signals Cash Flow Confidence
detail:
OLLI's New $500M Buyback Authorization Signals Cash Flow Confidence
Zacks Equity Research

OLLI
WMT
BJ

Trading disclosure

Ollie's Bargain Outlet Holdings, Inc.'s OLLI board of directors has authorized an additional $500 million for share repurchases, signaling management's confidence in the company's ability to generate substantial cash flow across diverse retail environments. The new authorization brings the retailer's total available buyback capacity to approximately $561 million, including the amount remaining under its previous authorization.

The latest reported numbers support that confidence. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Ollie's generated $108.1 million in cash from operating activities, up from $80.7 million a year earlier. For the first half, operating cash flow reached $153.6 million compared with $109.4 million in the prior-year period. Cash and investments totaled $507.1 million at quarter-end with no meaningful long-term debt.

The company has also been putting money to work. It repurchased $84 million of shares in the second quarter and $137.3 million during the first six months. Ollie's fiscal 2026 outlook called for approximately $175 million in repurchases, up from the prior estimate of $125 million.

Since initiating its buyback program in 2019, the company has deployed approximately $679 million toward share repurchases while simultaneously funding new stores, supply-chain expansions and growth initiatives. The new buyback authorization offers financial flexibility to execute repurchases opportunistically via open market transactions.

Walmart and BJ's Wholesale Drive Shareholder Value

Walmart Inc. WMT continues to prioritize shareholder returns through its share repurchase program. In the first six months of fiscal 2027, Walmart repurchased 42.3 million shares for $5.1 billion, leaving $25.1 billion available under its $30-billion authorization approved in February 2026. Walmart generated $19,710 million in operating cash flow during the aforesaid period, up $1,358 million year over year. Despite higher capital spending, Walmart's continued buybacks highlight its capacity to balance shareholder returns with business investments.

BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings, Inc. BJ also remains committed to returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, BJ's Wholesale repurchased approximately 1.4 million shares for $124.1 million, bringing first-half repurchases to $330.7 million. At the end of the second quarter, BJ's Wholesale had $422.1 million remaining under its existing authorization. With second-quarter adjusted free cash flow reaching $265.5 million, BJ's Wholesale continues to balance buybacks with investments in club expansion and long-term growth.

title: Walmart to offer US associates 250-plus free prescription medicines
detail:
Walmart to offer US associates 250-plus free prescription medicines
From 17 November 2026 · Retail Insight Network
Shubhendu Vimal
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:23 AM CDT 2 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart will provide US associates with prescription medicines without charge from 1 January 2027, alongside specialist-care and paid-leave benefits.

The retailer plans to introduce its Zero Dollar prescription tier for US associates, covering more than 250 generic, brand-name, and specialty medicines.

The tier will include some insulin products and inhalers.

Walmart said it will also create a Rare Conditions Centre of Excellence for associates and dependants enrolled in most Walmart medical plans.

The programme aims to provide no-cost access to specialists for multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

Eligible people being evaluated for, or diagnosed with, one of these conditions will be able to receive an in-person specialist evaluation and treatment review, according to the company.

The programme will cover travel for the patient and an adult caregiver, with Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic among the facilities involved.

Walmart executive vice president and chief people officer Donna Morris said: "We are excited to share upcoming changes to our benefits during this Annual Enrollment season. We are adding even more ways for associates and their families to live better through comprehensive and affordable healthcare and benefits."

From 17 November 2026, Walmart will introduce paid neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) leave.

Eligible associates whose children are admitted to a NICU within the first 28 days after birth and receive inpatient care will be entitled to up to 12 weeks of paid leave.

The NICU leave can be combined with other time-off and leave benefits, including maternity and parental paid leave.

Walmart said frontline associates could receive up to 28 weeks of paid leave when the benefits are combined.

Last month, Walmart committed not to use customers' personal data, income, shopping history, or sense of urgency to set what they pay.

In a letter to customers and members, president and CEO John Furner said using this information "to charge them more would violate the EDLP promise our business model is built on. We won't do it".

EDLP refers to everyday low prices, the pricing principle Walmart had followed for more than 50 years.

"Walmart to offer US associates 250-plus free prescription medicines" was originally created and published by Retail Insight Network, a GlobalData owned brand.

title: Investors Are Paying More for Walmart Than Amazon. Here’s Why That Doesn’t Add Up.
detail:
Investors Are Paying More for Walmart Than Amazon. Here’s Why That Doesn’t Add Up.

WMT
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) has opened a fulfillment center of more than 900,000 square feet in Stockton, California. The site uses automation and machine learning to cut the usual 12-step order process down to five. It will also employ about 1,000 people. The company says its next-generation fulfillment centers, of which Stockton is the fifth, will enable it to reach 95% of the U.S. population with next-day or two-day shipping when combined with the rest of its network. The stock closed more than 2% higher on October 8, its fourth straight gain. Beyond its push for faster delivery, Walmart's defensive appeal remains a key attraction for investors. But which other companies joined WMT on our list of the 10 Best Bear Market Stocks to Invest In Right Now?

Investors Are Paying More for Walmart Than Amazon. Here's Why That Doesn't Add Up.
Automation Is Changing Walmart's Business

I believe Stockton is just one piece of a much bigger shift. Walmart's U.S. e-commerce sales have grown more than 20% for 10 straight quarters, and fast deliveries jumped 48% last quarter. CFO John David Rainey said much of Walmart's recent spending has gone into supply chain automation and speed. That spending is also lifting higher-margin businesses. Advertising rose 38% last quarter, and membership fee revenue hit a record. Faster delivery brings more shoppers online, which feeds those businesses.

Still, Walmart remains a retailer at heart. Its stock fell 9% after its August report, despite beating estimates and raising its outlook. The decline reflected slow comparable sales and a soft Q3 guide, with operating income expected to grow just 2% to 4% as Walmart puts tariff refunds back into lower prices. Walmart's short-term margin pressure hasn't stopped hedge funds from backing the retail giant. See why WMT ranks No. 3 among the 10 Best Dividend Kings to Buy According to Hedge Funds and which other stocks made the list?

Walmart Costs More Than Amazon

Walmart's stock trades at a premium to its historical norms. The forward non-GAAP P/E of 37.48x sits about 24% above its 5-year average. That's even higher than Amazon, which trades at about 31x despite also owning AWS, a fast-growing, high-margin cloud business. The forward Price-to-sales ratio of 1.14x is also about 28% above its average. Yet analysts expect EPS to grow only 9% this fiscal year, about 12% in each of the next two, and 7% in fiscal 2030. Even based on fiscal 2030 earnings, the P/E would be around 28x. As of July 31, Walmart carried approximately $38.9 billion in net debt, excluding lease obligations. In my view, the automation story is big, but the stock already prices in a lot of it.
